newsitem.title: FRANCE: France calls off CIC sale.
newsitem.headline: France calls off CIC sale.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday that he had decided to call off the sale of the CIC banking unit of state-owned insurer Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN).

He said that the independent privatisation commission had ruled that an offer by Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) complied with the government's requirements while it had rejected an offer by Societe Generale.
He said he had decided to abandon the privatisation process in view of public and staff reactions to the sale. However the government remained determined to sell CIC in the future.
"After serious reflection the government has decided to call off the privatisation process for CIC," Arthuis told a news conference.
"It seemed important that everyone had the necessary time for reflection," he said. However, CIC still needed an association with a group capable of providing it with funds for its development.

"There is no question of not privatising CIC," he said. However he had been concerned by the fact that there was only one offer on the table after the privatisation commission ruled in a first stage that Societe Generale's bid did not comply with government requirement.
Arthuis also reiterated criticism of the heads of both GAN and CIC for their public comments on the privatisation.
"The managers of GAN and CIC did not behave in a way to encourage progress in this process," he said.
He declined to comment when asked whether the head of CIC, Bernard Yoncourt, would be replaced.
